text.p: Six people have been arrested in Ho Chi Minh City in connection with a racket that police said sent prostitutes from Vietnam to Singapore, an anti-vice squad officer said on Tuesday.
"We have arrested quite a number of women traffickers, including foreigners," the official told Reuters. "They are more sophisticated so it's more difficult for us to uncover."
He said the group had already sent three women to Singapore and was making arrangements for another nine.
The official daily Sai Gon Giai Phong named the six people, who included one Hong Kong Chinese man and another who was carrying a Singapore passport.
The four others were Vietnamese women who acted as intermediaries in selecting the prostitutes and organising their tourist visas for Singapore, the newspaper said.
It said that the Hong Kong man paid the Singapore man S$2,000 ($1,400) for each woman. The Singapore man then paid each intermediary S$300 per woman.
Once in Singapore, the women would earn S$400 per client at discotheques and pay the Hong Kong man S$2,000 every month, the newspaper said.
